title: Maternity Home — Minimum Requirements
notes: The section opens with a cross-reference: 'Other requirements are as stated under "Minimum requirements for all types of Health Institutions"' (page 26) — those common requirements are covered by the all-institutions module and are not duplicated here. Layout note: the 'Furniture' list on page 29 sits between the 'Nursery intensive care unit' equipment list and the 'Postnatal Ward' heading at the same indentation as the Nursery sub-headings; it has been placed as a subsection of Nursery, which is the most faithful reading of the layout.

items.requirement: Adequate ventilation and lighting provided by both natural and artificial means
Foot operated receptacle with self-closing devices, with plastic lining for ease of cleaning and infection control purposes
Patient trolley with mattress and side rails
Wash hand basin: connected to running tap water; splash back tiles; liquid soap; non-reusable hand drying facilities (i.e. paper towels)

items.reviewReason: The manual states 'Hydrocortisone x vials' — the number of vials is missing (compare '50% Dextrose x 2 vials', 'Adrenaline x 2 vials'); the required quantity cannot be determined from the source text.

items.reviewReason: 'Sluice room' appears as the final bullet under the Postnatal Ward 'Equipment' list, but it is a room/facility rather than equipment; the manual's placement is ambiguous as to whether it belongs to the Postnatal Ward equipment schedule or is a separate facility requirement.

items.requirement: Arrangement for transportation of patients with complications to nearest hospital
At least 2 midwives who are on permanent employment
items.quantity: at least 2 midwives, on permanent employment

items.requirement: The centre should be covered by a Gynaecologist
PCNs and nurse aides should not do deliveries
items.reviewReason: The manual phrases this prohibition with 'should not' ('PCNs and nurse aides should not do deliveries'), which under the obligation-word convention maps to RECOMMENDED, yet the content reads as a prohibition; the intended obligation strength (recommended practice vs mandatory prohibition) is unclear from the source wording.
